He was also seen by the ENT doctor and treated for vertigo by his primary care physician earlier.

clinician.final_diagnosis: The angiographic results revealed moderate disease of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery, occlusion of the left vertebral artery at its ostium, severe stenosis of 80-90% in the right vertebral artery at the proximal segment, and an EF of 55-60%.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old male initially presented to a cardiologist on November 3, 2021, with palpitations, leg cramps, fatigue, dizziness, and loss of balance. Orthostatic hypotension was ruled out, and he had previously been treated for vertigo. On August 16, 2023, he reported worsening episodes of dizziness, loss of balance, and fatigue. Subsequently, angiographic results on October 3, 2023, revealed moderate disease of the left anterior descending (LAD) artery, occlusion of the left vertebral artery at its ostium, severe stenosis of 80-90% in the right vertebral artery at the proximal segment, and an ejection fraction (EF) of 55-60%. An MRI performed on November 9, 2023, showed generalized cerebral atrophy but no acute CVA, mass lesion, or midline shift.
